subject: memphisToucan
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: toucan.
Style: Memphis Group 1980s design.
reasoning:
I'm picturing a Memphis Group-style toucan with bold colors, squiggles, terrazzo patterns, and black-white stripes against pastel pink/teal/yellow, planning to build it skeleton-first with a rest pose standing around 0.55 m tall on the ground.

I'm working out the rest pose with wings slightly spread, a tail, and a split beak, while deciding which helper functions to import from the builder library and whether to skip extra kits like glow. I'm settling on a Memphis palette of black, white, hot pink, teal, yellow, blue, orange, and lilac, imagining a black body with confetti terrazzo paint, a textured white bib, a huge striped beak with a black tip, and a Memphis-style decal eye, then starting to lay out the skeleton beginning with the hip root and spine chain.

Now I'm sketching the body as an upright tilted egg shape with coordinates for the tail base, chest, neck, and head, plus figuring out leg proportions—hip, knee, and ankle positions with bend lengths so the legs look properly bent and short enough to match the toucan's low stance.

I'm thinking through the zygodactyl toe structure, two toes forward and two back, each attached as simple joints off the ankle tip with capsule rods running from foot to tip, keeping it to single-segment toes for simplicity.

For the body, I'm defining a spine chain running from hips up through the neck using catmull points, rooting the hips joint and aligning the first spine joint to match the hips location so the chain starts cleanly.

Okay, settling on concrete coordinates now: hips at the base, rising through two spine points to the chest, then a neck base and head base point above. The body chain uses three named spans (spine1, spine2, chest) running through a smooth curve from hips to chest, parented at the hips joint.

For the neck I'm placing three control points between the chest and head base to form two spans (neck1, neck2), parented off the chest joint. Then I'm positioning the head joint itself near the skull, figuring out an aim direction that angles the beak forward and slightly downward from the head base point.

Now I'm working out a helper for local head offsets using forward/up/left parameters, then moving on to sweep the body shape along the spine chain using a loft with stations defined by position, width, and height.

For the body sweep, I'm deciding to use a catmull path through the key points with associated bone chains covering the body and neck, since the head joint hangs off the neck's end and needs the path to follow through those joints correctly.

Now I'm working out the tail: a separate three-joint chain branching from the hips that curves back and down behind the body, kept flat like feathers with a wide-but-thin elliptical cross-section rather than a round one.

I'm adding a radius function that tapers the tail toward a narrower tip, plus color bands for a Memphis-style accent (ending in a dark band) and a touch of red to echo the toucan's vent patch. For extra richness I'm considering fanning several extruded feather shapes out from the base of the tail to give it a layered, textured look, drawn as outlines extending backward along the tail's angled plane.

Working out the orientation math for each feather extrusion...

I'm planning the tail fan with five Memphis-style feathers in alternating teal, pink, yellow, blue, and orange, each a leaf-shaped extrusion with gradient color bands based on position. For the wings, I'm keeping them separated from the body and extended outward at roughly 35 degrees in a T-pose-like rest position rather than folded in.

Now I'm defining the wing skeleton as a shoulder-elbow-wrist-tip chain extending sideways and slightly back, sized for about a 0.45m wingspan to match a toucan's proportions, then placing secondary feather extrusions along the arm's trailing edge and primary feathers fanning out from the wrist.

I want the feathers to feel like Memphis-style bold geometric flat shapes, so I'm cycling each flight feather through bright pink, teal, yellow, and blue tints like a rainbow stripe pattern, defining them as rounded leaf-shaped outlines. Writing feather helper function...

I'm realizing the wing span is too wide for a toucan's real proportions, so I'm rescaling the shoulder, elbow, and wrist joint positions inward to tighten the overall span closer to 0.58.

Defining the arm chain joints...

Head sphere gets positioned forward and up, sized for scale. For the eye, I'm designing a decal with concentric rings — bare skin patch, yellow ring, black pupil, highlight — plus a white throat bib, Memphis-style with a pink squiggle eye ring.

Now for the beak, the real signature feature: I'm sweeping a tapered path from the head front curving down to a pointed tip, with elliptical cross-sections shrinking toward the point...

Still defining beak proportions...

I'm setting up the lower mandible as a thinner jaw-hinged piece, then coloring the whole beak with bold Memphis-style bands — black, pink, yellow, teal, orange, black tip — wrapped around the beak's length for a playful toucan look.

I'll build a custom zigzag function to create toothed edges on the bands, giving a sawtooth Memphis look around the beak sweep, using the same paint pattern shared across upper and lower beak. I'm also considering adding an SVG squiggle decal onto the beak surface for extra texture.

Now I'm planning the head paint scheme: black cap and nape, white-yellow cheeks and throat, with a confetti terrazzo effect using sparse cell-based polygons for pink and teal specks on the black body.

For the chest, I want a yellow-cream bib with a zigzag edge, placing a Memphis-style decal with squiggles, triangles, and circles over the pale background. The rump gets a hot pink confetti treatment, and I'm settling on a deep black-navy body with cream-yellow bib and red undertail colors.

Writing body paint logic...

Still building the radius interpolation helper...

Checking spine segments: spine1 to chest between P0-P3, then neck chain at P3-P4, head joint at P4. Working out where legs sit relative to the body's underside -- the body hovers around 0.19m up, so legs need roughly that much length to reach the ground.

I'm reconsidering overall proportions since toucan legs are quite short in reality; shifting the whole body down by about 0.05 and redefining the spine points with a base offset so the head top lands near 0.58 and legs show about 0.1-0.17 visible, plus adding a feathered thigh shape to cover the hip area.

For the legs themselves, I'm chaining hip (hidden inside body) to knee (hidden thigh) to ankle, using a thick tarsus sweep with tapering radii, and coloring them a Memphis-style teal-blue to match a toucan's leg tone.

Now I'm setting up the zygodactyl toes off each ankle joint—two forward tips and two backward tips with radius and small black claw spikes—named per side and index. Then I'm linking the leg chain's parent joint to the spine, and preparing to build the skull/eye detail on the head joint.

Working out the head and beak proportions now: placing the skull center slightly above and forward of the head joint, checking total body height against real toucan proportions, and tracing the beak's base point forward from the skull where the upper beak begins to emerge.

Now I'm shaping the beak's curve with a bezier arc—rising slightly for the culmen before dipping down to the tip—aiming for an exaggerated 0.30-length beak in Memphis style, and tapering the cross-section radii from thick at the base to thin at the tip.

The tip positions look fine with the upper beak overhanging the lower, consistent with toucan anatomy. Now I'm setting up a helper function to compute head-relative coordinates for positioning beak points relative to the head joint.

I'm now working out the joint hierarchy—defining the jaw joint parented to the head with an aim direction, then realizing I need to establish the head joint itself first, parented to the last neck joint, and double-checking the neck joint naming and count before wiring up the head's position and orientation.

For the lower beak, I'm defining a bezier curve from a base buried in the skull to a tapered tip, with radii shrinking toward the point, painted to match the upper beak and tolerating some overlap between them. I'm also planning the throat and jaw underside as cream-colored skin, and sketching out the eye placement on the side of the skull with a bold Memphis-style design—big blue iris, pink ring, black pupil with a white sparkle highlight, and a small yellow ring—applied as a decal.

Now I'm working out how to position the eye decal precisely using azimuth and elevation angles relative to the skull surface, letting the hit point's normal set the decal's direction automatically. I'm also considering adding a small raised ring around the eye using a torus shape in pink to give it some dimensionality beyond a flat decal.

For the head's color scheme, I'm mapping out a Memphis-style zigzag boundary: black crown and nape, cream cheeks and throat, trying to capture that classic toucan head pattern with sharp geometric edges instead of smooth gradients.

I'm also considering adding a playful flourish on top—maybe small Memphis-style triangle or cone shapes in pink and teal as a stylized topknot, since real toucans don't have crests but this is meant to be a design reinterpretation.

For the body, I'm planning terrazzo confetti patterning across the black torso and wing coverts, with the flight feathers reading as Memphis-style color stripes.

Writing feather color logic...

Actually simpler to cap at ~5 cached paints per feather color rather than one per feather, keeping chart count manageable. I'm now budgeting part counts: roughly 32 feathers per wing pair, plus tail, beak, and decal pieces, aiming for a total around 200-300 parts.

Legs and toes with claws, eyes, crest, thigh, and body stripes push the count toward 120, so I'm adding Memphis-style confetti scattered across the body — tiny cones, tori, and boxes in varied palette colors stuck onto the surface for a terrazzo effect, bumping the part count to around 60 more, still comfortably under a thousand total.

I'm sketching out the SVG texture set now: eye rings in blue/pink, a cream bib with squiggles and triangles, a transparent-background beak squiggle decal with black strokes and white dots, and a card-based fluffy feather texture in pink to scatter on the thigh.

For the remaining textures, I'm adding a Memphis triangle "mantle" decal on the back with zigzag black-on-yellow stripes placed on the upper rear body, plus a black-and-white dotted band marking at the beak base to mimic a toucan's nostril stripe. That brings the total texture count to around five or six, which feels sufficient.

Now I'm writing the SVG eye structure as layered concentric circles -- a blue skin patch, dark ink outline, pink ring, yellow iris, dark pupil, and two white glint highlights -- with a dashed white zigzag ring added around the outside for extra detail.

For the bib, I'm sketching a rounded shield-shaped path in cream with an ink stroke, then layering decorative squiggles, triangles, dots, and confetti shapes on top to give it a playful decal feel.

Still writing decal shapes...

Now I'm moving on to the back panel SVG, sketching a diamond-ish shaped viewBox.

Adding a midrib and chevrons to the fluff shape, then thigh fluff cards and crest blades. Now I'm setting up the module imports from the builder SDK and defining base color constants, being careful to only import what's actually used since unused imports fail typecheck.

Writing zigzag and keyframe interpolation helpers...

Building out the skeleton joints...

Finishing the tail chain with three joints tapering down and back, then working out where to anchor the tail feather fan so it sits near the hips and extends backward and downward without dipping below ground level.

I'm deciding to skip a separate tail core and instead let the fan feathers themselves rest on a small rounded sweep at the base, colored with black, pink, and yellow bands to avoid z-fighting with duplicate geometry.

Now I'm planning five tail feathers spread across angles from -36 to 36 degrees, assigning colors symmetrically (teal, pink, yellow, pink, teal) with the center feather being longest.

Writing wing joint positions...

Writing feather helper function...

Still refining feather outline points...

I'm also working out the bone parameter typing, leaning toward using `any` to avoid import risk, and computing the orientation vector by crossing the up and back directions.

For wing feather placement, I'm figuring out how to position secondaries along the arm by sampling points at various fractions along its path and deriving the bone reference at each point.

Positioning each feather's angle and length behind the trailing edge, tapering slightly toward the elbow, with small width overlaps between neighbors and tiny offsets to avoid coplanar z-fighting.

For the primaries near the wrist/hand, I'm computing angled directions sweeping outward from about 8° to 80°, with the outermost feather pointing nearly sideways and lengths varying across the set to shape a natural wingtip outline.

I'm checking the overall wingspan against the body proportions -- adjusting the hand and primary offsets down slightly to bring the total span from 0.73 to a more balanced 0.65 relative to the body height.

Now I'm planning the covert feathers that sit on top of the flight feathers, deciding on a Memphis-style confetti palette: pink, yellow, and teal cycling across the secondaries, with coverts layered above in contrasting tones so the wing reads as distinct rows of color rather than a muddle.

Refining the tip-stripe paint approach...

Writing body paint logic...

Still defining color zones...

Adding the bib decal on top of the cream paint, sized slightly smaller so it stays inset, then shaping the skull sphere with scale adjustments to fit the head bone's local axes.

I'm reasoning through the surface and orientation defaults for decals on the skull part, using world axes scaling since no quaternion is given, then setting up the eye azimuth/elevation placement and starting on the cheek cream coloring.

For the cere, I'm considering adding a torus-shaped ring at the beak base to form the collar, scaling it into an ellipse to match the beak's cross-section and coloring it black at the appropriate position.

Now I'm working out precise coordinates for the skull and beak path—defining the head joint, skull center and radius, then plotting the upper beak curve from base to tip across several control points, giving a beak length of roughly 0.3 units reaching out to z≈0.48.

Working out the lower beak joint positions and checking that its top edge meets the bottom of the upper beak so the two halves align properly at the beak gap.

I'm adjusting the beak gap so the mouth doesn't look open at the very tip, tweaking the lower beak's curve points to lift gently near f0.26 and recalculating where the upper and lower centerlines meet around f0.22 to make sure the gap stays small and natural-looking.

Now defining the beak's color bands, starting with black at the tip...

Defining color bands...

I need to figure out which side of the tube corresponds to which angle, since the sweep frame's "up/clockwise" orientation determines where left vs right decals land, so I'll map s>0 to 270 degrees and s<0 to 90 degrees to keep both sides consistent for the nostril placement.

I'm sizing the decal frame with explicit direction and dimensions scaled to the beak, adding small sphere nostril stubs embedded into the surface, setting flat/point end caps for the beak sweep since the base is buried in the skull, and placing a thin ring at the beak's base where it meets the skull front.

Now I'm positioning that collar ring around the beak cross-section, scaling it slightly oval to match the beak's width and height, nudging it upward so it sits just above the skull emergence point without floating awkwardly, and picking a cream tone so it reads as a Memphis-style accent rather than blending into the beak color.

Next I'm working on a crown tuft made of a few blades rising from the back of the head, figuring out the root position relative to the skull center and the direction vector they should extrude along to sweep up and backward.

For the blades themselves, I'll create three feather shapes colored teal, pink, and yellow, rooted inside the skull with a shared surface normal, then move on to sketching out thigh fluff near the hip joint.

For the thigh I'm going with a Memphis-style stripe pattern of cream and pink since there's already a built-in stripes helper, which fits the toucan-leg aesthetic nicely without needing custom texture work.

Now I'm setting up the legs using a limb helper that takes hip and ankle positions plus a bend direction, building a chain from hip to knee to ankle with named joints and contact points for grounding. I'm placing the hip joint slightly inset into the body and working out how the knee should bend forward relative to that.

Then I'm sweeping the leg chain with a tapered profile and a blue-to-teal paint, followed by computing toe tip positions branching off the ankle point for the foot.

Adding toe capsules and claw spikes...

I need to fix the toe joint reference to use the last joint in the leg chain rather than a possibly-null tip, and add an ankle bump sphere for visual bunching. I'm also placing a decal on the back near the top of the body, figuring out the right surface position and orientation for it.

I'm also considering adding Memphis-style anklet rings around the legs using a torus or closed sweep loop around each joint for extra color detail.

Scattering confetti chips across the body surface, filtering to avoid the bib area and cycling through small cone, torus, disc, and box shapes with varied colors.

I'm skipping beak dots and eyebrow details for now. Adding a thin torus ring around the eye for an eyelid effect, rotated to sit flush against the surface via `stick`.

Now I'm working through the sweep API parameters for constructing the body geometry.

Writing path and bone configuration...

Checking the body bottom position against leg length and ground placement looks fine, and now I'm verifying the shoulder point sits correctly on the body ellipse at that section of the curve.

Since rx and ry are nearly equal for the ellipses, the exact axis orientation of the chest front decal doesn't matter much—I'm just placing it at the front surface point along the curve where the chest widens.

I need to adjust the bib paint edge and decal placement so the cream shape and pink band overlap correctly on the chest without conflicting with the black base color, tweaking the decal's position and size slightly smaller and centered higher so it sits properly within the bib region.

Now I'm checking the back decal and considering whether body sectors should use the paint function instead of decals. For the tail, I'm working out logic so pinkish undertail coloring applies where the normal's y-component is low, falling back to black with confetti elsewhere, mirroring the rump and undertail rules already used in the body paint.

Still working out tail feather geometry...

The outline polygon stays convex so smoothing should be safe, and the typing for outline points should work fine. For the fluff cards, I'm scattering points across the thigh surface with minimum distance and normal filtering, then placing feather cards with sizing, lean, bend, and flow parameters tied to the thigh bone.

For the neck, I'm considering a ring of pink fluff cards forming a ruff collar around the base, positioned using a frame along the neck chain with outward-facing orientation -- though I should check the height doesn't creep up too close to the face.

I'll alternate the fluff texture between pink and teal variants, and add a small Memphis-style cheek decal with a squiggle and triangle below the eye. That gives me seven textures total to draw. Now starting on the SVG generators, beginning with the eye.

Writing bib SVG shape...

Still writing SVG shapes...

Now I'm scaling the fluff stroke width proportionally for the larger size, then thinking through decal placement for eyes using the skull's spherical coordinates with null-safety, and working out the toe capsule geometry to make sure the lowest point touches the floor plane correctly.

Adjusting toe tip positions to eliminate a tiny 2mm floating gap, and tilting the claw spikes slightly downward so they sink naturally into the floor without overshooting the 2% tolerance. The overall model height comes out around 0.67 with the crest included, which stays within acceptable sink limits, and I'm keeping the crest length modest at 0.07 to avoid visual clutter.

For the leg, I'm working through the joint placement between hip, knee, and ankle, trying to get the intertarsal joint to bend backward realistically like a real bird's leg rather than forward, which means reconsidering whether to use two or three segments for the visible lower leg and adjusting segment lengths accordingly.

Checking side conventions for hips and wing chains, then setting up the jaw joint relative to the head using local-space helper offsets, with the upper beak attached to the skull bone.

Now I'm defining the beak's numeric curve functions returning angle pairs, confirming how stick parts attach to sweep frames, and starting the body paint function with color constants and an edge-zigzag calculation based on surface normal and position.

Checking the tail coverts zigzag boundary and the hip pink region look fine, and confirming the mix function output is compatible with the color input type.

Now I'm working on the head paint function: crown black with a zigzag edge, a yellow stripe band below it, black on the back of the head, and cream elsewhere with pink-tinted chin shading based on surface normal.

I'm adding sparse teal/pink confetti dots on the cheeks and cream thigh stripes, then defining toe angle ranges for front and back feet with slightly different lengths.

For the toe tips, I'm computing endpoint positions from the base joint plus direction and length, carefully wrapping the limb points as THREE.Vector3 instances, then drawing each toe as a tapered capsule with a two-radius profile and paint color tied to the toe bone.

For claws I'm adding a spike at the tip oriented along the toe direction, plus a small heel ball sphere at the ankle. Then I'm sketching a set of small chip geometries (cone, torus, cylinder, box) meant to be scattered as surface detail, oriented along the local normal.

I'm filtering raycast hits onto the body surface for scattering those chips, landing on roughly 26 pieces, then tallying up the full part count across body, tail, skull, eyes, beak details, crest, tail feathers, and wings to get a sense of total piece complexity.

Since the target is around 180-340 parts, I'm padding out the wing structure with extra covert rows, alula feathers, and tail upper coverts, plus adding cheek confetti chips and toe pad segments to push the count higher.

Now I'm adding small teal triangle chips above each eye for brow stripes, and decorative white dot spheres swept along the upper beak ridge for extra texture.

I'm also considering serrated triangle teeth along the beak's mouth line, but the sweep's `along` function only samples the dorsal angle, so I'll need to adjust the angle parameter to get the underside positions right.

Now I'm sketching out the wing construction loop, setting up a mirrored chain of shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand joints for both sides using Catmull-Rom interpolation and parenting them to the chest.

Wait, if I reuse bodyPaint on the arm, the bib-detection logic would wrongly tint the front-facing wing surfaces cream instead of dark -- I need a dedicated wing paint function with its own confetti-on-dark coloring scheme instead.

Still writing feather placement code...

Still writing primary feather code...

Now I'm tallying up the total feather count per wing - arm coverts, secondaries, greater and median coverts, primaries, primary coverts, and the alula, roughly 32 per wing doubled for both sides. Adding up the rest of the bird: tail feathers with sweep, the body and skull, eyes with lids and decals, beak details including teeth and nostrils, and legs with toes still to account for.

Running the total across all the chip decorations, confetti scatter, cuffs, and ornamental bands brings the piece to roughly 220 elements overall.

Setting up the module imports and core utility functions...

Still writing feather paint logic...

Now I'm structuring the toucan build function itself, setting up the builder, defining feather outlines and tip colors with contrast against the pink/ink palette, then composing the skull and eye parts.

For eyes, I'm placing a decal on each side of the skull using angular offsets, then adding a thin torus eyelid ring embedded slightly into the surface around the decal edge, sizing the torus radius to match the decal's footprint and checking that the beak geometry doesn't overlap the eye placement.

Adjusting the eye position to az 78, el 6 to minimize beak overlap, and bumping the skull radius slightly to .06 for better proportion. Now I'm setting up the cheek decal placement and the beak ring geometry using a torus scaled along one axis, then starting to work out the ruff's neck attachment point.

For the ruff, I'm generating a ring of joints around the neck at a given point, then attaching feather cards in pink and teal that lean outward along the flow direction to create a collar effect. I need to make sure the ring's radius and plane orientation match the neck's tangent frame so the feathers sit naturally against the surface rather than clipping into it.

Checking the vertical placement, the collar sits above the chest decal so there's no overlap, and I'm settling on a tilt and lean combination so the feathers angle down and outward nicely.

Writing the band color definitions...

Still working through band boundaries...

Checking hip joint placement relative to spine, confirming the bone hierarchy and roles for legs, digits, wings, tail, jaw, head, neck, and spine chains, then sketching the thigh sphere geometry parameters.

Now I'm working out the crest feather placement using head-local coordinates with a specific normal direction, and verifying the beak construction using bezier curves for the upper and catmull-rom splines for the lower jaw.

Defining tapered sweep radii...

Writing confetti color helper and type definitions...

I'm checking the card and scatter function signatures, confirming how hits, rng seeding, and filtering options work for placing fluff on the thigh and confetti chips on the skull, cycling colors from the CONF palette as I finalize the code.

Now I'm working out the ring placement along the neck chain and setting up a feather-generation helper that computes direction, normal, and tangent vectors for extruding feather shapes with bevels and tip coloring.

I also need to add arm confetti scatter effects filtered by surface normal, and orient the tail feathers with a slightly tilted horizontal plane using a specific direction vector.

For the tail layer I'm setting base offset, angle spread, blue coloring, and feather length. I need to make sure joints like hips, body, neck, head, jaw, tail, wings, and legs are all created before the geometry that depends on them, and that the wing chain's parent joint exists first. For legs I'm passing an array of Vector3 points directly as the chain path, plus setting a contact offset.

Now I'm adding the eyelid geometry as a thin rotated torus. With everything in place, I'm ready to write the final code compactly but completely.
